stem: In which scenario might a clinician prioritize Montelukast over an inhaled corticosteroid as a preventer?

options.text: When the child is under 1 year of age and cannot use a spacer.
When the child has significant allergic rhinitis and the parents have concerns about steroids.
When the child has life-threatening asthma and requires maximum therapy immediately.
When the child only experiences symptoms once every six months.

explanation: The source identifies allergic rhinitis and parental steroid concerns as valid reasons to consider this oral alternative.
rationale: This oral medication is favored when there are barriers to using inhalers or when comorbid nasal allergies are present.

optionExplanations.A: Montelukast is generally only recommended for children above 2 years of age in specific circumstances.
optionExplanations.B: The source identifies allergic rhinitis and parental steroid concerns as valid reasons to consider this oral alternative.
optionExplanations.C: In life-threatening cases, inhaled corticosteroids are the priority, often at higher doses, rather than switching to an oral antagonist.
optionExplanations.D: Infrequent symptoms typically do not require any daily preventer therapy at all.

source.hint: This oral medication is favored when there are barriers to using inhalers or when comorbid nasal allergies are present.
